blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Information concerning national security, sovereignty, and foreign relations is strictly exempt from RTI disclosures.
Trade secrets, intellectual property, and Cabinet papers are legally protected from public disclosure.
Personal information that invades individual privacy is withheld under standard RTI provisions.
Matters concerning corruption and human rights violations are explicitly excluded from exemptions and must be disclosed.

blocks.content: Information related to corruption and human rights violations is NOT exempt.

items: Examiners often trick candidates by listing 'corruption' or 'human rights violations' as exempt—remember, they are NOT exempt.
Cabinet papers are specifically protected under RTI exemptions until a decision has been taken and the matter is complete.
Sovereignty and foreign relations are absolute grounds for exemption under RTI provisions.

blocks.content: IMPORTANT: Information related to corruption and human rights violations is NOT exempt.
